ai.description: The Nicobar Island frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is brown with a prominent dark mask, a white upper lip, and long, slender limbs. Distinctive features include a sharp snout and a pair of dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana nicobariensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored dorsolateral fold extending from the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: The Nicobar Island Frog inhabits tropical rainforests and freshwater swamps, typically found near streams or ponds at low to moderate altitudes across the Nicobar Islands.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar Island frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and invertebrates among the leaf litter of its tropical forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana nicobariensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in small, temporary pools. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with clutches containing dozens of eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nicobar Island frog is found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, typically inhabiting low-elevation forests and wetlands near sea level.
ai.callDescription: The Nicobar Island Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "chuck" notes, typically heard emanating from shallow pools and marshes within forested habitats.
